weapontypes.name: Aklys
weapontypes.notes:
A small club attached to a cord so that it can be thrown and retrieved.

After it is thrown, a 10% action will retrieve the weapon.

weapontypes.name: Atlatl (Launcher)
weapontypes.notes:
A wooden device used to hurl light javelins and spears. The Australian aborigine version is called a woomera. The atlatl was the precursor to the bow and arrow, and was capable of bringing down a woolly mammoth. For the record, a modern atlatl can launch an aluminum dart over 800’. The woomera may also be used as a club in melee.

Preparation time: 60%

weapontypes.name: Atlatl (Melee)
weapontypes.notes: A wooden device used to hurl light javelins and spears. The woomera may also be used as a club in melee.

weapontypes.name: Axe (woodsman's)
weapontypes.notes: Normally used as a tool

weapontypes.name: Bardiche
weapontypes.notes: An axe blade mounted on a pole.

weapontypes.name: Bastard Axe (1-H)
weapontypes.notes: An axe midway in size between the battle axe and the hand axe. The bastard axe can be wielded one-handed or two-handed.

weapontypes.name: Bastard Axe (2-H)
weapontypes.notes: An axe midway in size between the battle axe and the hand axe. The bastard axe can be wielded one-handed or two-handed.

weapontypes.name: Bastard Sword (1-H)
weapontypes.notes: A long, straight sword midway in size between the long sword and the two handed sword. The grip is almost long enough so that the weapon may be grasped with both hands; thus it is also called the hand-and-a-half sword.

weapontypes.name: Bastard Sword (2-H)
weapontypes.notes: A long, straight sword midway in size between the long sword and the two handed sword. The grip is almost long enough so that the weapon may be grasped with both hands; thus it is also called the hand-and-a-half sword.

weapontypes.name: Battle Axe
weapontypes.notes: A broad-bladed axe on a wooden haft. Typically with a blade on one side and a beak on the other, although some are bladed on both sides and some have a thrusting spike. Generally used two-handed.

weapontypes.name: Baw
weapontypes.notes: Can be used as an ice axe.

weapontypes.name: Beaked Axe
weapontypes.notes: An axe-bladed polearm with a beak on the front and back and a thrusting spike.

weapontypes.name: Bec de Corbin
weapontypes.notes: A polearm with a hooked, edged beak, a hammer head, and a thrusting spike. The beak is used to cut through armor.

weapontypes.name: Blackjack
weapontypes.notes: Used in ambush only

weapontypes.name: Blow Gun (Large)
weapontypes.notes:
A tube designed for shooting small darts. The dart is fired by blowing into the pipe. The darts are usually poisoned, but may be used without poison to hunt small birds.

Any poison on dart is injected on a critical result.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Tiny critical.

Preparation time: 90%

weapontypes.name: Blow Gun (Medium)
weapontypes.notes:
A tube designed for shooting small darts. The dart is fired by blowing into the pipe. The darts are usually poisoned, but may be used without poison to hunt small birds.

Any poison on dart is injected on a critical result.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Tiny critical.

Preparation time: 70%

weapontypes.name: Blow Gun (Small)
weapontypes.notes:
A tube designed for shooting small darts. The dart is fired by blowing into the pipe. The darts are usually poisoned, but may be used without poison to hunt small birds.

Any poison on dart is injected on a critical result.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Tiny critical.

Preparation time: 50%

weapontypes.name: Boar Spear
weapontypes.notes: A staff with a pointed metal head used in melee; Can't push shaft up if impaled.

weapontypes.name: Bola
weapontypes.notes: A South American throwing weapon consisting of three weights joined together by cords. When thrown, it spins in the air and wraps around its target, entangling it.

weapontypes.name: Boomerang (Fighting)
weapontypes.notes: An Australian wooden throwing weapon. The fighting version flies straight when thrown and does not return

weapontypes.name: Boomerang (Returning)
weapontypes.notes: An Australian wooden throwing weapon. Returns to thrower if it misses. A 10% action is required to catch it.

weapontypes.name: Boyheukz
weapontypes.notes:
The boyheukz (literally, helm-sunder'') is a favored missile weapon of the Mountain Folk, a crossbow-like weapon whose hurled stones will rive annor and hammer skulls. It is in almost all respects fashioned identically to the crossbow, save that it is intended to hurl stones or bullets rather than quarrels. The bowstring of an boyheukz is doubled when strung, and there is a window at the fore-end through which the stone will pass when the bow is loosed.

only Krush criticals. It is only slightly more difficult and time consuming to reload than the light crossbow (reload percentage activity if 180% ). To fire without penalty requires three rounds of preparation (OB suffers a -5 modification with only 2 rounds of preparation and a -20 modification with only 1 round of preparation). The stones for this weapon are actually metal bullets expressly crafted for the purpose and are carried in broad, shallow wallets at the Dwarfs belt .. Sling stones or other suitable ammunition may also be used (though OB will suffer a penalty of -I 0).

weapontypes.name: Broadsword
weapontypes.notes: A basic straight double-edged sword with a wide blade.

weapontypes.name: Buurik
weapontypes.notes: The buurik is perhaps the only non-mechanical bow used with any frequency by Dwarves. It is a composite bow, crafted in much the same fashion as those wielded by human hands, but much stronger (yet requiring far more painstaking effort in the fashioning).

weapontypes.name: Cabis
weapontypes.notes: Basically a throwing weapon.

weapontypes.name: Cat 'o' Nine Tails (Fighting)
weapontypes.notes:
A leather whip with nine thongs ending in metal barbs.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Tiny critical.

weapontypes.name: Cat 'o' Nine Tails (Penal)
weapontypes.notes:
A leather whip with nine thongs.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Tiny critical.

weapontypes.name: Cestûszak
weapontypes.notes: The Cestûszak is made of the hardest woods, layered and laquered as are all Dwarvish shields, bound with the strongest of metals and fitted with a spiked boss on the face and a well honed edge on a segment of the rim, to the fore of which a wielder's fist clutches the handgrip.

weapontypes.name: Claymore
weapontypes.notes: Scottish two handed sword

weapontypes.name: Club
weapontypes.notes: A large club for fighting in melee; generally used two-handed.

weapontypes.name: Comet Hammer
weapontypes.notes: A flail consisting of two spiked balls joined by a length of chain.

weapontypes.name: Composite Bow
weapontypes.notes: A medium-sized bow made of layers of wood, and possibly bone or metal.

weapontypes.name: Cudgel
weapontypes.notes: Large walking stick.

weapontypes.name: Cutlass
weapontypes.notes: A heavy short sword with a curved blade. Good, all purpose blade sturdy enough to cut ships’ riggings. The pirate’s weapon of choice, according to film and fiction.

weapontypes.name: Dag
weapontypes.notes: Very large curved sword

weapontypes.name: Dagger
weapontypes.notes: Typically, a straight double-edged fighting knife; however, it includes curved and single-edged knives of the appropriate size.

weapontypes.name: Dart (throwing)
weapontypes.notes:
A metal-tipped wooden throwing dart with feather flights.

Any poison on dart is injected on a critical result.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Tiny critical.

An attacker using darts can make two attacks in a round at -10 OB for each attack.

weapontypes.name: Dhurvab
weapontypes.notes: The dhurvab is a two-handed warhammer, a maul for use at war. Attacks with the dhurvab are resolved on the War Mattock Attack Table but only do Krush criticals. However, the wielder of a dhurvab suffers a -5 to initiative rolls on the round after delivering a critical. As with most hafted Dwarven weapons, the Dhurvnb is reinforced by rings of iron, steel or other metal.

weapontypes.name: Dirk
weapontypes.notes: Scottish Dagger.

weapontypes.name: Falchion
weapontypes.notes: A broad, curved sword. Legend has it that the Conyers Falchion was used to slay one of the last (if not the last) dragon in England in 1063. The Conyers Falchion is on display in Durham Cathedral.

weapontypes.name: Fauchard
weapontypes.notes: A long, thin blade mounted on a pole. The edge is on the inside curve of the blade.

weapontypes.name: Flail
weapontypes.notes: One to three metal heads attached to a long wooden handle by chains.

weapontypes.name: Foil
weapontypes.notes: A fencing sword that does not have an edge on the blade. The blade has a square cross section and a sharp tip. It is only used for thrusting attacks. Generally used for dueling.

weapontypes.name: Ge
weapontypes.notes:
Treat any criticals as both K and G.

If fumbled, roll a DG on thrower.

weapontypes.name: Gheløst
weapontypes.notes:
The gheløst is a flail with two heads, each slightly larger than those of a traditional flail with a somewhat longer length of chain binding them to the haft.

When used in combat, roll two separate attacks (one for each of the weapon's heads). The second attack roll has a special modification of -I 0. Either or both heads may fumble in their attack.

weapontypes.name: Glaive
weapontypes.notes: A long knife-bladed polearm.

weapontypes.name: Great Sword
weapontypes.notes: A larger, heavier version of the two-handed sword.

weapontypes.name: Guisarme
weapontypes.notes: A hook-bladed polearm.

weapontypes.name: Handaxe
weapontypes.notes: A medium-sized, one-handed single-bladed fighting axe.

weapontypes.name: Hand Crossbow
weapontypes.notes:
A low power, pistol sized crossbow. The string can be drawn back with one hand. The hand crossbow is an extremely rare weapon usually only found in the hands of well to do assassins.

Preparation time: 100%

weapontypes.name: Harpoon (light)
weapontypes.notes:
A barbed spear with a rope attached. The harpoon is usually used for hunting large marine animals.

The rope enables the harpooner to draw the victim closer when a critical is rolled. The chance the harpoon will remain embedded each round is 15% x critical level (A crit is 15%, B crit is 30%, etc). Intelligent creatures can try to remove the harpoon or cut the rope.

Preparation time: 150%.

weapontypes.name: Heavy Crossbow
weapontypes.notes: A heavy, powerful bow which requires mechanical means to draw the string.

weapontypes.name: Heavy Spear
weapontypes.notes: The lance when used on foot.

weapontypes.name: Hup
weapontypes.notes: The hup is a weapon much like a whip that is worn about the waist, often doubly or trebly looped, as a belt. The buckle and clasp provide the hilt and tip of the weapon, for they are fashioned to fit together in order to secure the hup as a garment. The hup may be slid free of its wearer's waist and uncoiled in one smooth motion. If the weapon obtains a 'C' critical or higher in combat, there is a 75% chance that the target will also suffer an additional Tiny critical of 2 severities less from the clasp point.

weapontypes.name: Hûrcka
weapontypes.notes: The Hûrcka is similar to a flanged mace, save that the flanges are brought out into claws alongside the head. It is a slow weapon, and somewhat unwieldy. Its bearer suffers a -3 to initiative rolls. However, it inflicts gruesome wounds in combat, combining the crushing impetus of a mace or club with the gouging effect of wicked claws. Orcs love it.

weapontypes.name: Irgaak
weapontypes.notes: Roll criticals twice, apply all results.

weapontypes.name: Javelin
weapontypes.notes: A light throwing spear.

weapontypes.name: Jitte
weapontypes.notes:
A Japanese metal baton with a large tine for catching swords. Used by police to subdue unruly warriors.

+10 to disarm maneuver.

The jitte has a shield bonus versus melee weapons of +15. (Only if the weapon is not used to attack or if 100% of OB is used to parry.)

weapontypes.name: Jo (1-H)
weapontypes.notes: Japanese staff.

weapontypes.name: Jo (2-H)
weapontypes.notes: Japanese staff.

weapontypes.name: Katana (1-H)
weapontypes.notes: A Japanese curved, single edged, long sword usually used two handed. Said by some to be the most perfect blade ever produced. The katana is not like a long sword in traditional western sword play; it is traditionally wielded as a “single strike” weapon. The attacker makes one single quick, lethal strike.

weapontypes.name: Katana (2-H)
weapontypes.notes: A Japanese curved, single edged, long sword usually used two handed. Said by some to be the most perfect blade ever produced. The katana is not like a long sword in traditional western sword play; it is traditionally wielded as a “single strike” weapon. The attacker makes one single quick, lethal strike.

weapontypes.name: Knife
weapontypes.notes: A small fighting knife made of steel. This weapon usually has small guards. The blade may be straight or curved, and single or double edged. Sharp, well-honed kitchen knives also use this attack table.

weapontypes.name: Kynac
weapontypes.notes: A great throwing dagger.

weapontypes.name: Kyotetsu-shoge
weapontypes.notes: A Japanese combination weapon used by the Ninja. The Kyotetsu-shoge consists of a knife with a hook blade joined to an iron ring by a rope woven from human hair. The knife or iron ring may be thrown or swung and retrieved by the rope. It may also be used as a grappling hook. Retrieving this weapon after it is thrown takes 10% of the character’s action that round.

weapontypes.name: Lance
weapontypes.notes: A heavy spear used from a running horse. It can be sharpened or unsharpened, and the weight is variable.

weapontypes.name: Lance (medieval)
weapontypes.notes: If jousting, all criticals are 'A's.

weapontypes.name: Lasso
weapontypes.notes:
A rope with a noose at one end. The noose is thrown to encircle and hold an opponent.

A critical results that indicate an effect for a number of rounds require that the weapon continue to be employed for that period (to maintain the hold). New attack rolls are not required to maintain the hold. At the end of the period the target will be free from the hold. If the attacker ceases employing the weapon or ends the hold, the critical effect ends and the weapon may then be used to make another attack.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Grapple critical.

Preparation time: 150%

weapontypes.name: Light Crossbow
weapontypes.notes: A bow where the string is drawn using a lever, a hook attached to the belt, or by pulling with both hands.

weapontypes.name: Long Bow
weapontypes.notes: A powerful bow made from a single long piece of wood, ideally yew. Surviving examples of late medieval and renaissance English long bows have draw weights between 98 to 185 lbs.

weapontypes.name: Long Kynac
weapontypes.notes: A great long dagger.

weapontypes.name: Long Scimitar
weapontypes.notes: A longer and heavier version of the scimitar.

weapontypes.name: Long Sword
weapontypes.notes: A straight bladed, double-edged sword, slightly longer and narrower than a broadsword.

weapontypes.name: Lucerne Hammer
weapontypes.notes: A polearm with a hammer head, a hooked beak and a long thrusting spike.

weapontypes.name: Mace
weapontypes.notes: A flanged, metal head on a wooden haft.

weapontypes.name: Main Gauche
weapontypes.notes: long dagger with a large basket hilt and hand guard that can catch opponent’s weapons.

weapontypes.name: Man Catcher
weapontypes.notes:
An unusual polearm in which the arms of the head encircle the target so that the target can be held.

A critical result that indicates an effect for a number of rounds requires that the weapon continue to be employed for that period (to maintain the hold on the target). New attack rolls are not required to maintain the hold. At the end of the period, the target will be free from the hold. If the attacker ceases employing the weapon or ends the hold, the critical effect ends and the weapon may then be used to make another attack.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Grapple critical.

weapontypes.name: Military Fork
weapontypes.notes: A polearm attached to two flared, sharp spikes. The pitchfork reborn as a military weapon. (Yes this weapon really did exist.)

weapontypes.name: Morning Star
weapontypes.notes: One or more heavy spiked, metal balls attached to a wooden handle, often by a chain.

weapontypes.name: Mullet
weapontypes.notes:
A medium-sized fish. (Reasonably fresh and raw.)

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Subdual critical.

*Fumbles: All mullet fumbles have the following result:
The mullet squirms out of your grasp. Next time, use a dead fish.

weapontypes.name: Nagamaki
weapontypes.notes: A heavy Japanese battle weapon consisting of a wide, curved blade mounted on a haft. Favored by the mountain warrior monks.

weapontypes.name: Naginata
weapontypes.notes: A short, curved Japanese blade mounted on a pole. The naginata can be used as a spear, but can also inflict sweeping cutting attacks. Traditionally used by Samurai women.

weapontypes.name: Narnûn
weapontypes.notes: The namun is another two· handed crushing weapon. It is a long-hafted, flanged mace, less commonly used than the dhurvab but wielded enough to warrant attention. It is a formidable sight indeed to see a company of Dwarf Namunemerrin advancing across some cavern floor, deep in the earth, clad in plate armor and wearing full helms bearing the semblence of horrid beasts. It is also typically the last thing ever seen if the observers are Orcs or Goblin folk.

weapontypes.name: Net (fishing)
weapontypes.notes:
A tough rope net. The net is used to entangle opponents and can be thrown.

A Critical result that indicates an effect for a number of rounds requires that the weapon continue to be employed for that period (to maintain the hold). New attack rolls are not required to maintain the hold. At the end of the period, the target will be free from the hold. If the attacker ceases employing the weapon or ends the hold, the critical effect ends and the weapon may then be used to make another attack.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Grapple critical.

weapontypes.name: Net (gladiator's)
weapontypes.notes:
A tough rope net with metal weights around its edge. The gladiators’ net is used to entangle opponents and can be thrown.

A Critical result that indicates an effect for a number of rounds requires that the weapon continue to be employed for that period (to maintain the hold). New attack rolls are not required to maintain the hold. At the end of the period, the target will be free from the hold. If the attacker ceases employing the weapon or ends the hold, the critical effect ends and the weapon may then be used to make another attack.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Grapple critical.

weapontypes.name: Ninjato (1-H)
weapontypes.notes: A curved Japanese single-edged sword slightly shorter than the katana. The Ninja used this blade because it was easier to carry than a katana when sneaking or performing acrobatic maneuvers. Less athletic Japanese nobles also wielded the ninjato, unlike the samurai, who used the heavier katana.

weapontypes.name: Nodwick
weapontypes.notes:
Nodwick represents the typical henchbeing. Add +10 to the attack roll for each chest, sack or heavy backpack the henchman is burdened with.

*Fumbles: All henchbeing fumbles have the following result: All containers that the henchbeing is carrying shatter on impact, showering everyone with their contents. Fragile items break on impact.

All combat ceases immediately and a feeding frenzy ensues, as everyone in the immediate area begins grabbing loot. Combat does not resume until all loot has been retrieved. With a successful Self Discipline roll, a combatant may use the frenzy to make an unobtrusive, strategic withdrawal from the battlefield. (i.e. run away.)

weapontypes.name: No-Dachi
weapontypes.notes: A long Japanese two-handed sword.

weapontypes.name: Nunchaku (1-H)
weapontypes.notes: Oriental peasant weapon developed from a flail used to thresh rice.

weapontypes.name: Nunchaku (2-H)
weapontypes.notes: Oriental peasant weapon developed from a flail used to thresh rice.

weapontypes.name: Partisan
weapontypes.notes: A broad-bladed spear named after the light troops that used it.

weapontypes.name: Pick
weapontypes.notes: Normally used as a tool.

weapontypes.name: Pike
weapontypes.notes: A long, heavy spear used by foot soldiers in formation against cavalry.

weapontypes.name: Pilum
weapontypes.notes: Roman throwing spear.

weapontypes.name: Pitchfork
weapontypes.notes: The classic farmers pitchfork

weapontypes.name: Polearm
weapontypes.notes: An axe-bladed pole arm with a beak and a thrusting spike.

weapontypes.name: Pole Axe
weapontypes.notes: A heavy axe mounted on a pole.

weapontypes.name: Quarterstaff
weapontypes.notes: Commonly used fighting staff, often with the ends shod in metal.

weapontypes.name: Ranseur
weapontypes.notes:
A spear with tines that can catch armor or weapons.

+10 to disarm maneuver.

weapontypes.name: Rapier
weapontypes.notes: A long, straight double-edged fencing sword.

weapontypes.name: Rope Dart
weapontypes.notes:
Chinese throwing knife with a cord attached so that it can be thrown or swung and then retrieved.

Retrieving a rope dart after it is thrown takes 10% of a character’s action for that round.

An attacker can make two attacks per round when using a rope dart. Each attack receives a -10 penalty to its OB.

Large and Super Large criticals may not be obtained from a Tiny critical.

weapontypes.name: Sabre
weapontypes.notes: Curved sword used from horseback

weapontypes.name: Sai
weapontypes.notes:
Oriental peasant weapon developed from the trident used in rice planting. Principally employed to block swords, the sai may also be thrown. Usually used in pairs.

+10 to disarm maneuver

The sai as a shield bonus versus melee weapons of +25 (only used if the weapon is not used to attack or if 100% of OB is used to parry).

weapontypes.name: Scimitar
weapontypes.notes: Oriental and Middle Eastern curved single-edged sword.

weapontypes.name: Shang
weapontypes.notes: Parrying weapon, +30 vs. melee if not used to attack.

weapontypes.name: Short Bow
weapontypes.notes: A bow made from a single short piece of wood.

weapontypes.name: Short Sword
weapontypes.notes: A short, straight double-edged sword.

weapontypes.name: Shuriken
weapontypes.notes:
Small oriental throwing knives.

Any poison on shuriken is injected on a critical result.

An attacker can make two attacks per round when using shuriken.
Each attack receives a -10 penalty to its OB.

Large and Super Large criticals can not be obtained from a Tiny criticals.

weapontypes.name: Sling
weapontypes.notes: A leather pouch in the middle of a cord. A stone is placed in the pouch and whirled around the thrower’s head. Then one of the cords is released so that the stone flies off toward the target.

weapontypes.name: Soshad (Melee)
weapontypes.notes: The soshad is another Dwarven missile weapon, this one a type of staff sling. Fashioned and used like any other staff sling, the soshad is different in its haft, which is a stout length of wood bound by rings of hammered metal. Its ferrule (ring or cap on the end of the shaft) is fluted and pointed, designed so as to be useable as a spear in times of need without being damaged, blunted or overly battered by the wear it would certainly encounter as the tip of a staff. The soshad can be used as either a sling or as a spear.

weapontypes.name: Soshad (Sling)
weapontypes.notes: The soshad is another Dwarven missile weapon, this one a type of staff sling. Fashioned and used like any other staff sling, the soshad is different in its haft, which is a stout length of wood bound by rings of hammered metal. Its ferrule (ring or cap on the end of the shaft) is fluted and pointed, designed so as to be useable as a spear in times of need without being damaged, blunted or overly battered by the wear it would certainly encounter as the tip of a staff. The soshad can be used as either a sling or as a spear.

weapontypes.name: Spear
weapontypes.notes: A staff with a pointed metal head used in melee.

weapontypes.name: Staff Sling
weapontypes.notes:
A sling attached to a staff. This gives the sling more leverage, enabling the wielder to launch larger missiles.

May be used to launch objects such a flasks. Preparation time: 80%

weapontypes.name: Steel Whip
weapontypes.notes: Chinese whip made of seven steel segments with a point at both ends. The steel whip can be swung or whipped at the opponent.

weapontypes.name: Three Section Staff
weapontypes.notes: Chinese weapon comprised of three short staves linked together.

weapontypes.name: Tiger Claw
weapontypes.notes: Chinese metal rake that is strapped to the hand and forearm.

weapontypes.name: Tiger Hook
weapontypes.notes:
Chinese weapon with a small hooked blade and a large guard for parrying.

Has a shield bonus versus melee weapons of +15 (only used if the weapon is not used to attack or if 100% of OB is used to parry.)

weapontypes.name: Tomahawk
weapontypes.notes: American indian small axe

weapontypes.name: Tonfa
weapontypes.notes: Okinawan rice husking rod.

weapontypes.name: Trident
weapontypes.notes: A three-pronged fork best known for its use by gladiators.

weapontypes.name: Trogn
weapontypes.notes: The trogn is a short (not for Dwarves, of course) pole-hammer, crafted with two opposing beaks and a spike at the end

weapontypes.name: Tunch
weapontypes.notes: The tunch is used both as a weapon and as a pointed hammer to chip rock. Most Gnolls possess one, whether they are skilled at using it in melee or not.

weapontypes.name: Two-Handed Sword
weapontypes.notes: A large, straight double-edged battle sword.

weapontypes.name: Typh
weapontypes.notes: If fumbled, roll a “DK” on thrower.

weapontypes.name: Töshma
weapontypes.notes: The Töshma is a truly Orcish sword. Shaped somewhere between a scimitar and falchion, the first six inches of the blade are generally crafted to resemble snarling teeth (this is ornamental and does not affect the weapon in combat). Only the first foot of the top or spine of the weapon is actually sharpened, and even then not always. It is difficult to master and easy to lose in a fight, as it is a heavy one-handed weapon. Persons attacking in the snap action phase suffer an additional -10 penalty to that which is normally incurred. Those making a deliberate attack gain an additional +5.

weapontypes.name: Wakazashi
weapontypes.notes: A Japanese curved single-edged short sword.

weapontypes.name: War Fan
weapontypes.notes: Sturdy metal fan generally used as a club. It is very effective for defense, because it is used to cause confusion in opponents and can parry missile attacks.

weapontypes.name: War Hammer
weapontypes.notes: A metal hammerhead with a beak opposite mounted on a wooden haft.

weapontypes.name: War Mattock
weapontypes.notes: A heavy battle weapon developed from the mattock.

weapontypes.name: Whip
weapontypes.notes: A long whip made of braided leather.

weapontypes.name: Yarkbalka
weapontypes.notes: If fumbled, roll a “CS” on thrower.
